beats.vo: This is Groundtruth, a Chrome extension for home buyers. On a realestate.com.au unit listing, it reads only the address, never the listing, and proves which home it is.
beats.caption: [[Chrome extension]] · reads only the address, never the listing
beats.action: Real REA unit listing loads; panel slides in; Verified home strip turns green.

beats.vo: The Verified home strip opens into the address match receipt: what it read, the normalised address, the G-NAF ID, and four of four checks passed.
beats.caption: [[Address match]] receipt: read → normalised → G-NAF id · 4/4 checks
beats.action: Click the strip; receipt expands; cursor walks read / normalised / g-naf / checks.

beats.vo: Second card, the one listings never show: what can legally rise next door. Today's buildings, with glass wherever planning rules allow two or more extra storeys. Here, {{nextDoorLotsSpoken}} lots within a hundred metres could rise {{nextDoorStoreysSpoken}} more.
beats.caption: What can [[legally rise next door]]: glass = planning headroom
beats.action: 3D card in view; toggle a map layer; hover the headroom glass.

beats.vo: Below that, Microburbs API data where it exists: risk overlays, strata levies, and the Microburbs value range. Anything unavailable collapses into one line.
beats.caption: [[Microburbs API]]: risks · strata · value, where available
beats.action: Scroll Risk overlays → Strata levy → Microburbs value; collapsed 'unavailable' line.

beats.vo: On Domain, listings change in place without a page load. Groundtruth notices, drops the stale answer, and the receipt updates to the new home.
beats.caption: In-place listing switch: stale answer [[dropped]], receipt updates
beats.action: Domain listing → click a similar listing in place; receipt re-reads the new address.

beats.vo: Some listings hide the unit number. Groundtruth won't guess. It shows the building, asks how many bedrooms, and narrows the list when the buyer taps one.
beats.caption: Hidden unit: no guessing. Tap [[bedrooms]] to narrow the building
beats.action: 417-419 Bourke St (Building state) → tap 2 → unit list narrows.

beats.vo: In Bondi, outside the City of Sydney pilot, it says so plainly, and makes no data call at all.
beats.caption: Bondi: out of area, said plainly, [[no data call]]
beats.action: Bondi listing → grey Out of area state.

beats.vo: At an inspection? Press play for a thirty-second spoken briefing of everything on the panel.
beats.caption: 30-second spoken [[briefing]]
beats.action: Back on the EXACT home; press the briefing button; captions follow the audio.

beats.vo: Does the address match hold up? We froze {{heldOutNSpoken}} real listings before testing. {{wrongHomesSpoken}} wrong homes. The exact home in {{exactRateSpoken}} of them, and {{outOfAreaSpoken}} out-of-area listing caught.
beats.caption: {{heldOutN}} held-out real listings: [[{{wrongHomes}} wrong homes]] · exact {{exactRate}}

still.name: accuracy-demo
still.heading: [[Address match]] on {{heldOutN}} held-out real listings
still.note: Labels frozen before the run · eval/FROZEN.md · eval/results.md

beats.vo: Limits. Agency quoting data is rarely available, so we don't lean on it. The Microburbs value covers about thirteen percent of homes. Building heights from OpenStreetMap are estimates. And it's City of Sydney only, for now.
beats.caption: Limits, stated plainly

still.name: limits
still.heading: Limits
bullets: City of Sydney's 29 suburbs only, for now

beats.vo: Groundtruth. Built on the Microburbs API: G-NAF matching, planning controls, valuations. Ready to drop into any property extension.
beats.caption: Built on the [[Microburbs API]] · ready for any property extension
beats.action: Panel on the first listing; end card follows.
